transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (Aurum CTO), Priya Patel (Head of Infrastructure), Marco Diaz (Security Lead), Sofia Kim (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand Aurum's requirements for a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood inference. Key topics covered: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region/data residency constraints (EU-first), CIDR overlap concerns, SSO/KMS/compliance needs, ded vs hosted tradeoffs, pilot plan and next steps.

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Alex from Redwood. we have Maya our solutions engineer as well. quick intros?
[00:00:08] Liam: Liam O'Rourke, CTO at Aurum Finance, hi.
[00:00:11] Priya: Priya, head of infra.
[00:00:13] Marco: Marco, security.
[00:00:15] Sofia: Sofia, devops.
[00:00:18] Maya: Hi all, glad to be here. quick agenda - understand your infra, constraints, and what a pilot would look like.

[00:01:05] Alex: high level - are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private? where are you leaning?
[00:01:12] Liam: We're leaning Private/VPC. we can't send any PII outside EU regions, and our legal requires dedicated network controls. we've used managed endpoints before but need network isolation and auditability.
[00:01:32] Alex: got it, private makes sense. can you give us a sense of traffic patterns? latency targets? throughput needs?
[00:01:40] Priya: for chat assistants, 80% of queries are sub-1s internal SLOs but external facing should be <350ms ideally. token volumes are spiky - month end reporting causes bursts.
[00:01:55] Sofia: also, we do batch embeddings for analytics overnight - large throughput but latency not critical.

[00:02:30] Maya: good - that shapes deployment. For Private we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink (private endpoints), and dedicated clusters in your VPC or in our VPC with cross-account peering. which is your preferred pattern?
[00:02:45] Priya: we prefer customer-hosted endpoints inside our VPC or cross-account peering to avoid internet egress and to ensure logs stay in our AWS account. PrivateLink is attractive for simpler connectivity but we need to check SNI/service limits.
[00:03:03] Marco: security question - how does key management work? can we bring our own KMS/HSM, and do audit logs include per-request identifiers?
[00:03:12] Maya: yes, we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) via AWS KMS - you can provide grant policies. audit logs include request id, model, latency, and token counts. logs can be forwarded to your CloudWatch/Elastic stack. small note, sometimes our product doc refers to 'KV cache' as K-V cash in transcripts, sorry for typos in docs.

[00:04:00] Alex: region constraints? you mentioned EU-only. which AWS regions are acceptable?
[00:04:06] Liam: eu-west-1 is primary; we can allow eu-central-1 as backup. no US regions for production. pilot could be in eu-west-1 only.
[00:04:20] Maya: that's fine. we have ded nodes in eu-west-1, and private deployment options for that region. note: some open models we host are only available in us-east-1 due to licensing; we'll flag model availability per region.

[00:05:10] Priya: networking specifics - our VPCs use RFC1918 10.0.0.0/16 and 172.16/12 for other accounts. we already have Transit Gateway between prod and analytics VPCs. overlapping CIDR across partners has been a pain. how do you handle overlap?
[00:05:30] Maya: we can support cross-account peering and Transit Gateway attachments. if CIDR overlaps we usually recommend: 1) use PrivateLink (endpoint services) so you avoid peering routes; 2) run a Redwood VPC in your account (we can provide AMIs) which avoids peering; or 3) use NATed egress through a dedicated routing plane. each has tradeoffs.
[00:05:58] Liam: PrivateLink sounds appealing to avoid route table complexity. what's the performance impact?
[00:06:05] Maya: PrivateLink adds minimal latency (~5-15ms typical) but for high-throughput low-p99 targets peering or in-account is better. Also PrivateLink is cross-AZ but you hit ENI limits per region if you scale aggressively - we can request quota increases.

[00:07:00] Marco: on compliance - can you send SOC2 and pen test reports? Also we need SAML SSO integration with Okta, RBAC, and audit trails retained 1 year.
[00:07:10] Alex: yes, we'll share SOC2 and our latest pen-test summary. SAML/SSO with Okta is supported, RBAC via SCIM/Okta provisioning is available. Audit retention is configurable; we can push logs to your account so retention is under your control.

[00:07:40] Sofia: one more thing - egress to S3 for model artifacts and to external model hubs, will that traverse our VPC?
[00:07:48] Maya: artifacts are pulled during model provisioning. if private, we can set up VPC endpoints (S3 VPC endpoint) so traffic stays within AWS. For public model pulls we usually stage artifacts into your S3 bucket or use a signed transfer.

[00:08:30] Liam: about dedicated vs hosted - what's the cost delta and operational responsibility?
[00:08:36] Alex: Hosted API is simplest and cost-effective for variable workloads. Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity in our infra and some isolation. Private (VPC) means either we deploy into your VPC or you deploy our runtime; cost varies with reserved nodes and support tier. I'll send a pricing matrix.

[00:09:20] Priya: if you deploy into our VPC, what components run inside vs outside? we want control plane in our account or at least control plane traffic not to traverse public internet.
[00:09:31] Maya: two patterns: 1) Control plane in Redwood (hosted) with a private control plane option over a PrivateLink endpoint so control traffic terminates into your VPC. 2) Full private control plane where you run the control plane components in your environment (on-prem or account) - that one is heavier. For most customers we do a hybrid: customer data plane in their VPC (inference nodes and logs), and control plane still in Redwood but accessible via private endpoint.

[00:10:20] Marco: For auditability we prefer control plane events to also be logged to our S3 or SIEM, is that possible?
[00:10:28] Maya: absolutely - we can forward control plane audit events to your CloudWatch or Kinesis stream; we also support pushing them into your SIEM.

[00:11:05] Alex: any blockers on networking side for a pilot in eu-west-1?
[00:11:12] Priya: we need to validate ENI quotas and confirm no CIDR overlap with partner accounts. I'll take that action item.

[00:11:40] Liam: performance concerns - we might need p99 under 450ms for customer-facing chat. can you support that with regional private deployment?
[00:11:50] Maya: yes, with local dedicated nodes and ensuring requests route to eu-west-1 and with prefix/KV cache warmed we'll see sub-400ms p50 and p99 depends on sequence lengths. we'll include suggested instance types and batching configs in the playbook.

[00:12:30] Sofia: how are model updates rolled out? we need canary deploys and ability to rollback quickly.
[00:12:36] Maya: rollouts are first-class: canaries, A/B, auto-fallback to older model variants if latency or error rates spike. We expose routes per-model-version so you can pin traffic.

[00:13:20] Marco: encryption in transit - do you support mutual TLS?
[00:13:25] Maya: yes, mTLS for node-to-node and mutual auth for private endpoints is supported. For client-to-endpoint we support TLS; mutual TLS can be configured if you provide certs.

[00:14:10] Alex: ok quick recap - pilot in eu-west-1, PrivateLink or in-account deployment depending on CIDR overlap, SOC2 docs and KMS details to be shared, and a technical deep-dive next week. any other asks?
[00:14:28] Liam: can you include a perf benchmark for our prompt patterns?
[00:14:33] Maya: yes we'll include a perf checklist and we'll run a small benchmark during the pilot.

[00:15:00] Priya: also network diagram with IP ranges and suggested endpoints please.
[00:15:05] Alex: will do.

[00:30:00] [longer discussion happened, talking through Transit Gateway vs PrivateLink tradeoffs - transcript clipped for brevity in the notes but included below]
[00:30:10] Maya: if you run Transit Gateway, a peering model gives lowest latency but you need to manage route tables; PrivateLink simplifies route management but costs slightly more. also if you fear CIDR collisions, PrivateLink avoids them.
[00:31:05] Priya: what's the expected operations overhead for in-account deployment?
[00:31:12] Maya: in-account we provide AMIs/k8s manifests and a hardened distro; you'll manage upgrades but we provide automated tooling and a maintenance window process. support tiers include managed upgrades option.

[00:40:00] Marco: one last question on data residency - we need contractual language to guarantee EU-only storage for production.
[00:40:10] Alex: we can add contractual clauses specifying region constraints for production data and encryption keys staying in EU. legal will follow up.

[00:44:00] Alex: thanks everyone - we'll send the artifacts and schedule the deep-dive.
[00:44:07] Liam: thanks, appreciate it.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
